relevance_note: Family report of four TNFAIP3 carriers with named individual detail: 'A heterozygous c.1727dupC variant in the TNFAIP3 gene (NM_006290) ... was identified in the Pt1 and her mother (Pt 4)'.
method_note: Hand extraction from text and Table 1 (patients as rows, one row per manifestation; labels 'Pt 1'..'Pt 4' in the table, 'Pt1'..'Pt4' in the text, the text form used). The father ('a relative (father)' in figure legends; NGS was done on 'Pt1 and her parents') is included as 'father of Pt1' with no variant row: the paper never states his genotype explicitly. 'consanguineous patients' in the Abstract appears to mean blood relatives, not parental consanguinity, so consanguinity is 'not reported'. Vital status left 'not reported' (not stated). Age at onset 'Early childhood (less than 2 years)' given no ISO value (upper bound only). Age at thyroiditis/T1D diagnosis recorded as feature onset, not as HA20 diagnosis age. Zygosity 'heterozygous' for Pt2/Pt3 rests on 'The same frameshift mutation' plus the Abstract statement about the four patients; inheritance 'inherited maternal' for Pt1-3 because their mother Pt4 carries the same variant. Recurrent fever excluded for Pt1, Pt2, Pt4 from 'Only Pt3 presented with recurrent episodes of fevers' (named group). For Pt3, 'no autoimmune manifestation up to the age of 14' was used to exclude autoimmune thyroiditis, type 1 diabetes, autoimmune hepatitis and autoimmune cytopenia. Anti-TG 77 U/ml in Pt4 is below the stated normal value (<100) but the paper does not call it normal, so no row. Functional assays are stated for 'all the patients'/'all four patients' (Pt1-4); pSTAT1 increase in '3 out of 4' unnamed, not attributed. Contradictions/inconsistencies: Pt3 is '13 year-old' in Methods but 'no autoimmune manifestation up to the age of 14' in Results; Pt2 short stature '3° centile' (text) vs '3°-25° centile' (Table 1); Pt4 adult height '10-20° centile' (text) vs 'Short stature (10-25°)' (Table 1); Pt4 onset 'since childhood' (text) vs 'Early childhood (less than 2 years)' (Table 1). Table onset recorded.
